title: AI Service Authentication and Billing Readiness
summary: Prepare a provider API project with separate human and workload identities, least-privilege credentials, billing ownership, limits, monitoring, and tested rotation.
prerequisites: An approved provider, tenant or organization, and workload owner
A data classification and expected usage profile
Access to the provider's current authentication and billing documentation

sections.title: Separate enrollment, workload identity, and authorization
paragraphs: Human enrollment establishes the administrative and billing boundary. A human may create or join an organization, tenant, project, or workspace and assign owners. A production application should instead use a provider-supported workload credential or federated identity. Authentication identifies that workload. Authorization separately decides whether the authenticated identity may access the exact tenant, project, workspace, region, model, and operation.

Fictional worked case: `invoice-redactor-prod` processes restricted invoice text. Mira Chen owns human enrollment, Jon Bell owns the workload, and Priya Shah owns billing. Its fictional boundary is tenant `org_fictional_42`, project `proj_invoice_prod_42`, workspace `ws_finance_42`, region `fictional-region-1`, and environment `production`. It may use only `fictional-redactor-v1` for a redaction request. All names and identifiers in this case are fictional.

Secret custody is a separate control. The fictional credential is referenced as `secret://fictional/prod/invoice-redactor/api-key`, and only the production deployment identity may read it. Evidence may contain this reference, a fingerprint, ownership, scope, and rotation timestamps, but not the secret value. Do not place workload secrets in source code, browser clients, container images, logs, tickets, or personal accounts.

The simulator below fails closed. Only a well-formed credential with status `active` can authorize. A credential that is `staged`, `failed`, `revoked`, unknown, missing a status, missing a required scope field, or scoped to another resource is denied. Staged readiness is deliberately separate from active authorization. Readiness permits a staged candidate to be checked without allowing it to serve requests.

Provider details are not interchangeable. OpenAI documents project API keys and Authorization-header authentication at https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/authentication. Anthropic documents the `x-api-key` header at https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/getting-started. Google documents Gemini API keys and their project relationship at https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/api-key. Mistral documents organization and workspace authentication, including workspace-scoped API keys and key lifecycle operations, at https://docs.mistral.ai/admin/identity-access/api-keys. For Meta Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Phi, NVIDIA, and Z.ai, check the exact hosted service, cloud deployment, gateway, or self-hosted endpoint. This resource does not claim equivalent keys, scopes, billing features, revocation behavior, or prices across those services.
sections.callout: Human enrollment creates an administrative boundary. Workload authentication identifies the application. Authorization permits only an active, well-formed credential for the exact recorded resource boundary.

code.label: fictional_readiness.py: offline readiness, authorization, spending-control, and rotation simulator
code.code:
from copy import deepcopy

# FICTIONAL FIXTURES ONLY. This program performs no network, provider,
# credential, secret-manager, or billing action.
REQUIRED_SCOPE_FIELDS = ("tenant", "project", "workspace", "region", "models")

FIXTURE = {
    "scenario": "FICTIONAL AND EXPECTED UNTIL EXECUTED",
    "workload": "invoice-redactor-prod",
    "tenant": "org_fictional_42",
    "project": "proj_invoice_prod_42",
    "workspace": "ws_finance_42",
    "region": "fictional-region-1",
    "model": "fictional-redactor-v1",
    "billing_owner": "Priya Shah",
    "secret_reference": "secret://fictional/prod/invoice-redactor/api-key",
    "budget": {
        "mode": "alert_only",
        "provider_documented_hard_stop": False,
        "approved_stop_test_passed": False,
    },
    "old": {
        "id": "cred_fictional_old_001",
        "tenant": "org_fictional_42",
        "project": "proj_invoice_prod_42",
        "workspace": "ws_finance_42",
        "region": "fictional-region-1",
        "models": "fictional-redactor-v1",
        "status": "active",
    },
    "replacement": {
        "id": "cred_fictional_new_002",
        "tenant": "org_fictional_42",
        "project": "proj_invoice_prod_42",
        "workspace": "ws_finance_42",
        "region": "fictional-region-1",
        "models": "fictional-redactor-v1",
        "status": "staged",
    },
}


def credential_is_well_formed(credential):
    if not isinstance(credential, dict):
        return False
    required = ("id", "status") + REQUIRED_SCOPE_FIELDS
    return all(isinstance(credential.get(field), str) and credential[field] for field in required)


def matches_scope(credential, fixture):
    if not credential_is_well_formed(credential):
        return False
    expected = {
        "tenant": fixture.get("tenant"),
        "project": fixture.get("project"),
        "workspace": fixture.get("workspace"),
        "region": fixture.get("region"),
        "models": fixture.get("model"),
    }
    if not all(isinstance(value, str) and value for value in expected.values()):
        return False
    return all(credential[field] == expected[field] for field in REQUIRED_SCOPE_FIELDS)


def authorize(credential, fixture):
    if not credential_is_well_formed(credential):
        return "DENY malformed or missing credential fields"
    if credential["status"] == "revoked":
        return "DENY revoked credential"
    if credential["status"] != "active":
        return "DENY non-active credential"
    if not matches_scope(credential, fixture):
        return "DENY wrong tenant or resource boundary"
    return "ALLOW fictional request"


def readiness(fixture, credential):
    if not isinstance(fixture.get("billing_owner"), str) or not fixture["billing_owner"].strip():
        return "BLOCK missing billing owner"
    if not isinstance(fixture.get("secret_reference"), str) or not fixture["secret_reference"].strip():
        return "BLOCK missing secret custody reference"
    if not credential_is_well_formed(credential):
        return "BLOCK malformed or missing credential fields"
    if credential["status"] not in ("staged", "active"):
        return "BLOCK replacement is not staged or active"
    if not matches_scope(credential, fixture):
        return "BLOCK replacement boundary mismatch"
    if credential["status"] == "staged":
        return "READY staged replacement candidate"
    return "READY active credential"


def hard_spending_enforcement(budget):
    if not isinstance(budget, dict):
        return "BLOCK hard spending enforcement unverified"
    if budget.get("mode") == "alert_only":
        return "BLOCK alert-only is not a hard spending cap"
    if budget.get("mode") != "hard_stop":
        return "BLOCK hard spending enforcement unverified"
    if budget.get("provider_documented_hard_stop") is not True:
        return "BLOCK hard-stop behavior lacks documentation evidence"
    if budget.get("approved_stop_test_passed") is not True:
        return "BLOCK hard-stop behavior lacks approved test evidence"
    return "VERIFIED documented and tested hard spending enforcement"


def activate_replacement(state):
    old = state["old"]
    replacement = state["replacement"]
    if old.get("status") != "active":
        raise ValueError("old credential must be active before cutover")
    if readiness(state, replacement) != "READY staged replacement candidate":
        raise ValueError("replacement readiness must pass while staged")
    replacement["status"] = "active"
    old["status"] = "revoked"
    return state


def fail_before_old_revocation(state):
    if state["old"].get("status") != "active":
        raise ValueError("old credential must remain active before revocation")
    if state["replacement"].get("status") != "staged":
        raise ValueError("only a staged replacement can fail before cutover")
    state["replacement"]["status"] = "failed"
    return state


def fail_after_old_revocation(state):
    if state["old"].get("status") != "revoked":
        raise ValueError("post-revocation recovery requires a revoked old credential")
    if state["replacement"].get("status") != "active":
        raise ValueError("active replacement required before post-cutover failure")
    state["replacement"]["status"] = "failed"
    state["fallback"] = "required"
    # There is intentionally no transition that restores the revoked credential.
    return state


def run_assertions():
    fixture = deepcopy(FIXTURE)
    old = fixture["old"]
    staged = fixture["replacement"]

    assert authorize(old, fixture) == "ALLOW fictional request"
    assert authorize(staged, fixture) == "DENY non-active credential"

    failed = deepcopy(staged)
    failed["status"] = "failed"
    assert authorize(failed, fixture) == "DENY non-active credential"

    unknown = deepcopy(staged)
    unknown["status"] = "unknown"
    assert authorize(unknown, fixture) == "DENY non-active credential"

    missing_status = deepcopy(staged)
    del missing_status["status"]
    assert authorize(missing_status, fixture) == "DENY malformed or missing credential fields"

    missing_scope = deepcopy(old)
    del missing_scope["project"]
    assert authorize(missing_scope, fixture) == "DENY malformed or missing credential fields"

    malformed = deepcopy(old)
    malformed["tenant"] = ["org_fictional_42"]
    assert authorize(malformed, fixture) == "DENY malformed or missing credential fields"

    wrong = deepcopy(old)
    wrong["tenant"] = "org_fictional_other_99"
    assert authorize(wrong, fixture) == "DENY wrong tenant or resource boundary"

    revoked = deepcopy(old)
    revoked["status"] = "revoked"
    assert authorize(revoked, fixture) == "DENY revoked credential"

    assert readiness(fixture, staged) == "READY staged replacement candidate"
    missing_owner = deepcopy(fixture)
    missing_owner["billing_owner"] = ""
    assert readiness(missing_owner, staged) == "BLOCK missing billing owner"

    assert hard_spending_enforcement(fixture["budget"]) == "BLOCK alert-only is not a hard spending cap"
    label_only = {
        "mode": "hard_stop",
        "provider_documented_hard_stop": False,
        "approved_stop_test_passed": False,
    }
    assert hard_spending_enforcement(label_only) == "BLOCK hard-stop behavior lacks documentation evidence"
    verified = {
        "mode": "hard_stop",
        "provider_documented_hard_stop": True,
        "approved_stop_test_passed": True,
    }
    assert hard_spending_enforcement(verified) == "VERIFIED documented and tested hard spending enforcement"

    before_failure = fail_before_old_revocation(deepcopy(fixture))
    assert before_failure["old"]["status"] == "active"
    assert before_failure["replacement"]["status"] == "failed"

    rotated = activate_replacement(deepcopy(fixture))
    assert rotated["old"]["status"] == "revoked"
    assert rotated["replacement"]["status"] == "active"
    assert authorize(rotated["old"], rotated) == "DENY revoked credential"
    assert authorize(rotated["replacement"], rotated) == "ALLOW fictional request"

    recovered = fail_after_old_revocation(rotated)
    assert recovered["old"]["status"] == "revoked"
    assert recovered["replacement"]["status"] == "failed"
    assert recovered["fallback"] == "required"


def main():
    run_assertions()
    fixture = deepcopy(FIXTURE)
    old = fixture["old"]
    replacement = fixture["replacement"]

    print("baseline authorization:", authorize(old, fixture))

    wrong = deepcopy(old)
    wrong["tenant"] = "org_fictional_other_99"
    print("wrong tenant:", authorize(wrong, fixture))

    print("staged replacement authorization:", authorize(replacement, fixture))
    failed = deepcopy(replacement)
    failed["status"] = "failed"
    print("failed replacement authorization:", authorize(failed, fixture))

    revoked = deepcopy(old)
    revoked["status"] = "revoked"
    print("revoked old credential:", authorize(revoked, fixture))
    print("replacement staged readiness:", readiness(fixture, replacement))

    missing_owner = deepcopy(fixture)
    missing_owner["billing_owner"] = ""
    print("missing billing owner:", readiness(missing_owner, replacement))
    print("budget enforcement:", hard_spending_enforcement(fixture["budget"]))

    rotated = activate_replacement(fixture)
    print("after activation readiness:", readiness(rotated, rotated["replacement"]))
    print("after activation authorization:", authorize(rotated["replacement"], rotated))
    print("rotation state: old={0} replacement={1}".format(
        rotated["old"]["status"], rotated["replacement"]["status"]
    ))

    recovered = fail_after_old_revocation(rotated)
    print("rollback after failure: BLOCK old={0} replacement={1} fallback={2} no_secret_resurrection=yes".format(
        recovered["old"]["status"],
        recovered["replacement"]["status"],
        recovered["fallback"],
    ))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

sections.title: Establish financial and operational controls before traffic
paragraphs: Assign technical and billing owners before enabling traffic. Record the payment, subscription, organization, project, or workspace boundary that receives usage. Also record approved models and regions, rate limits, request or token quotas, spend alerts, any actual spending-enforcement mechanism, alert recipients, log retention, support path, and credential rotation procedure.

A quota is not automatically a spending cap. Request-per-minute and token-per-minute controls ordinarily constrain rates or quantities over an interval. A budget might only send an alert. A real hard spending control requires documented blocking semantics and approved test evidence. The simulator therefore checks three separate facts: a `hard_stop` mode, provider documentation supporting that behavior, and a passed stop test. A label alone does not pass.

Provider-specific controls must be verified separately. OpenAI documents usage limits at https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rate-limits. Google documents Gemini billing, quotas, and limits at https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/billing#quotas-limits. Anthropic documents organization rate limits at https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/rate-limits. Mistral documents organization billing roles, payment and usage management, and a monthly cap under which access can be suspended at https://docs.mistral.ai/admin/billing-usage/billing. These references do not establish equivalent hard caps, quota units, prices, or controls for Meta Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Phi, NVIDIA, or Z.ai. In particular, the Mistral billing reference is not evidence of a universal instantaneous hard-stop guarantee.

Credential rotation is an enforced state transition. Begin with the old credential active and the replacement staged. Check the replacement's exact scope, billing ownership, and secret custody while it remains unable to authorize production requests. At cutover, activate the replacement and revoke the old credential. Then assert that the old credential is denied and the replacement is allowed.

If the replacement fails before old-key revocation, mark the replacement failed or revoked and leave the old credential active while the boundary is corrected. If failure occurs after old-key revocation, keep the old credential revoked. Stop traffic or use an independently approved fallback, audit usage, and issue a new replacement. Never restore, copy, or resurrect the revoked secret.

Independent changed-input task, to complete before reading the answer key: copy the fixture and set `billing_owner` to an empty string, set the replacement `tenant` to `org_fictional_other_99`, and set `budget.mode` to `hard_stop` while leaving both evidence booleans false. Predict the results of `readiness`, `authorize`, and `hard_spending_enforcement`. Then write the permitted credential states and the safest recovery steps. This task is independent because all three changes must be diagnosed rather than inferred from the worked output.
sections.callout: Do not equate a quota, alert, dashboard label, or configured budget with a tested hard spending stop.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Prerequisite for the offline exercise: Python 3 with its standard library. Save the first section's Python code exactly as `fictional_readiness.py`. From the directory containing that file, run `python3 fictional_readiness.py`. On systems where Python 3 is invoked as `python`, use `python fictional_readiness.py`. No package installation, provider account, network connection, real credential, secret-manager access, or billing action is required.

The program contains assertions that would catch the original lifecycle defect: staged and failed credentials must be denied by authorization. It also tests unknown status, missing status, missing scope, malformed scope, wrong tenant, revoked status, missing billing ownership, an alert-only budget, an unverified `hard_stop` label, failure before revocation, successful cutover, and failure after revocation. An assertion failure or nonzero process exit means the exercise did not produce the expected decisions.

Expected output, not a claim of actual execution:
baseline authorization: ALLOW fictional request
wrong tenant: DENY wrong tenant or resource boundary
staged replacement authorization: DENY non-active credential
failed replacement authorization: DENY non-active credential
revoked old credential: DENY revoked credential
replacement staged readiness: READY staged replacement candidate
missing billing owner: BLOCK missing billing owner
budget enforcement: BLOCK alert-only is not a hard spending cap
after activation readiness: READY active credential
after activation authorization: ALLOW fictional request
rotation state: old=revoked replacement=active
rollback after failure: BLOCK old=revoked replacement=failed fallback=required no_secret_resurrection=yes

Trace the worked decisions as follows. The baseline succeeds because the credential is active and every required scope field matches. The wrong-tenant case fails exact scope matching. Staged and failed replacements cannot authorize. The independently revoked copy is denied. The staged replacement can pass readiness without gaining authorization. Removing the billing owner blocks readiness. The alert-only budget fails hard-cap verification. Cutover changes observable state to old revoked and replacement active. A later replacement failure changes it to failed while the old credential remains revoked and fallback becomes required.

Answer key for the changed-input task: `readiness` returns `BLOCK missing billing owner` because the owner check fails first. If billing ownership is corrected but the wrong replacement tenant remains, readiness returns `BLOCK replacement boundary mismatch`. `authorize` denies the unchanged staged replacement as `DENY non-active credential`; changing it to active would still produce `DENY wrong tenant or resource boundary`. `hard_spending_enforcement` returns `BLOCK hard-stop behavior lacks documentation evidence` because the changed label lacks both required forms of evidence. Safe recovery is to stop launch, assign and verify a billing owner, issue or correct a staged replacement under `org_fictional_42`, verify all scope fields and secret custody, obtain documentation and approved test evidence for any claimed hard stop, and then perform cutover. If the old credential was already revoked, it remains revoked.

A real readiness review must make an approved minimal request from the deployed workload, verify attribution in provider usage and billing records, exercise a denied scope or model, inspect audit evidence, test alert delivery, and confirm the documented response to revocation and any spending stop. Record the provider, tenant, time, credential fingerprint, request identifier, response, attribution evidence, and billing or audit evidence while redacting secrets. The offline results cannot prove any provider behavior.

Provider-neutral transfer uses the same questions across OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Meta Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Phi, NVIDIA, and Z.ai: who owns enrollment and billing, what authenticates the workload, which exact resource boundary is authorized, where the secret is held, which quotas exist, whether spending is actually blocked, what telemetry proves attribution, and which rotation transitions are allowed. Implementations differ among hosted APIs, cloud marketplace deployments, gateways, and self-hosted endpoints. Verify the selected service's first-party documentation instead of treating this list as a feature-equivalence table.

Stop if a secret is exposed, billing is unowned, usage cannot be attributed, an administrator or personal secret is required, a request targets the wrong boundary, or an assumed limit lacks evidence. Revoke or restrict affected credentials, audit usage, preserve request identifiers, and route to a fallback only if that fallback's authorization and billing boundaries were independently approved.
sections.callout: All scenario records and output are fictional or expected until the learner runs the offline file. The exercise validates local decision logic, not provider authentication, billing, quota, alert, revocation, or spending behavior.

code.label: Credential rotation states and evidence rules
code.code:
FICTIONAL EXPECTED STATE MACHINE

NORMAL ROTATION
old=active, replacement=staged
  -> readiness checks exact tenant, project, workspace, region, model, billing owner, and secret reference
  -> replacement=active and old=revoked
  -> assert old authorization is denied
  -> assert replacement authorization is allowed

FAILURE BEFORE OLD REVOCATION
old=active, replacement=staged
  -> replacement=failed or revoked
  -> old remains active
  -> correct the boundary and create a new staged replacement

FAILURE AFTER OLD REVOCATION
old=revoked, replacement=active
  -> replacement=failed
  -> old remains revoked
  -> fallback=required
  -> stop or use an independently approved fallback
  -> audit usage, correct the boundary, and issue a new credential
  -> never resurrect or copy the revoked secret

HARD SPENDING EVIDENCE
mode=hard_stop is necessary but not sufficient
provider_documented_hard_stop=true is also required
approved_stop_test_passed=true is also required
otherwise the claimed hard stop is blocked as unverified

REAL EVIDENCE RULE
A real result requires a dated record of provider, tenant, request identifier, response, usage attribution, credential fingerprint, and billing or audit evidence. Secret values must remain redacted.
